import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_31/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_31/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_31/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_31_2 and Source3_31_0 on movie_id to get movie title with ratings and user_id
merged = pd.merge(source2, source0[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Join merged with Source3_31_1 on user_id to get gender info
merged = pd.merge(merged, source1[['user_id', 'gender']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Compute average rating grouped by title and gender
# Pivot the table to get separate columns for F and M average ratings
avg_ratings = merged.groupby(['title', 'gender'])['rating'].mean().unstack()

# Rename columns to match target schema
avg_ratings = avg_ratings.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'})

# Reset index to have 'title' as a column
avg_ratings = avg_ratings.reset_index()

# Ensure columns are in the order: ['title', 'F', 'M']
avg_ratings = avg_ratings[['title', 'F', 'M']]

# Convert ratings to float (they should already be float, but ensure)
avg_ratings['F'] = avg_ratings['F'].astype(float)
avg_ratings['M'] = avg_ratings['M'].astype(float)

# Save the result to the target path
avg_ratings.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_31_2 and Source3_31_1 on user_id
joined_user = pd.merge(source2, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_31_0 on movie_id
joined_all = pd.merge(joined_user, source0, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Compute average rating grouped by title and gender
# Pivot the table to get separate columns for F and M average ratings
avg_ratings = (
    joined_all.groupby(["title", "gender"])["rating"]
    .mean()
    .reset_index()
    .pivot(index="title", columns="gender", values="rating")
    .rename(columns={"F": "F", "M": "M"})
)

# The pivot may have missing values for some genders, keep them as NaN
# Reset index to have title as a column
result = avg_ratings.reset_index()

# Write the final output with exact column names as target schema
result.to_csv(
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/target_multisource_critique_history.csv",
    index=False,
)
